title: KL Rahul in Line for ODI Vice-Captaincy as Asian Games Clash Hits India's Plans
excerpt: With Shreyas Iyer leading India at the Asian Games in Japan, the vice-captaincy under Shubman Gill is open for the September 27 ODI series — and the second wicketkeeper slot has become a Pant vs Jurel debate.
body:
• KL Rahul is the front-runner to be named India's vice-captain for the three-match ODI series against the West Indies, with the squad to be picked in a selection meeting on September 16.
  • Regular vice-captain Shreyas Iyer will be unavailable as he leads India's T20 team at the Asian Games in Japan, which overlaps directly with the West Indies series starting September 27.
  • Ishan Kishan's Asian Games duty also forces a debate over the second wicketkeeper slot, with Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel the contenders — and the Irani Cup leadership hanging on the call.

KL Rahul is in line to be named India's vice-captain for the upcoming three-match ODI series against the West Indies at home, with the squads for the series and the Irani Cup to be finalized at a selection meeting on September 16, according to PTI. Regular ODI vice-captain Shreyas Iyer will be in Japan leading India's T20 side at the Asian Games, which overlap directly with the home series.

Asian Games clash forces the rethink

The scheduling conflict is the heart of the matter. The West Indies ODIs run from September 27 to October 3 — the first in Thiruvananthapuram, followed by Guwahati on September 30 and Mullanpur (New Chandigarh) on October 3 — while India's Asian Games cricket campaign runs from September 28 with the final on October 3. With Iyer captaining the T20 contingent in Japan, the vice-captaincy under ODI captain Shubman Gill falls open, and Rahul, the senior wicketkeeper-batter, is the natural stand-in.

The September 16 selection meeting carries extra weight. It will be attended by chief selector Ajit Agarkar, whose contract expires on October 4 — this is his final scheduled selection assignment under the current deal. He is eligible for a one-year extension, but the BCCI has stayed silent on his future, fueling speculation about the selection committee's leadership.

The second keeper question

With Iyer and Ishan Kishan both on Asian Games duty, the backup wicketkeeper slot behind Rahul is the other big call. The choice comes down to Rishabh Pant or Dhruv Jurel. "It is a choice between Pant and Jurel. Obviously, the head coach's and captain's points of view will be important," a BCCI source privy to selection matters told PTI.

The decision ripples into domestic cricket. If Pant misses out as second keeper, he is expected to lead the Rest of India side against defending Ranji champions Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup in Srinagar. Should Pant make the ODI cut, Jurel — who recently captained India A in Sri Lanka — would take the Rest of India leadership instead.

A Pant recall would be notable. He was dropped from the 50-over setup before the Afghanistan series in June and spent two years on the bench as Rahul remained India's first-choice keeper since 2024. The door opened because of the Asian Games absences, and with Virat Kohli returning to the ODI side — he now plays only the 50-over format, having retired from T20Is in 2024 and Tests in 2025 — the batting order has a settled, senior core around which the selectors can experiment.

Diaspora angle

The West Indies series is primetime viewing for the diaspora — a home series with day games at IST-friendly times for Gulf viewers and early-morning slots for North America. With Gill as captain, Kohli back, and a new-look attack featuring Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, and Prince Yadav, this is the first extended look at India's ODI core between World Cup cycles. Ruturaj Gaikwad is also expected back in the squad with Iyer's slot open.

What's next

The September 16 meeting, held a day after the second T20I against Afghanistan, will lock in both squads. Questions beyond the vice-captaincy: the second keeper call, Hardik Pandya's status as a seam-bowling all-rounder (he was named in the India A squad and is expected to be cleared for white-ball cricket from September 20), and the composition of a pace attack missing Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, and the Asia Games-bound seamers. India's Asian Games campaign itself begins September 28 — so for one October week, two Indian teams will be playing simultaneously on different continents.
